hints: 'Failed Registering Bundle Identifier' or 'cannot be registered to your development team'? The shipped com.nutai.app is already taken. Change the Bundle Identifier field to a unique string (com.yourname.nutai), then let Xcode retry. A free Apple ID works. 'No profiles for com.nutai.app were found' goes away once it registers.
No team in the list? Add your Apple ID first: Xcode → Settings → Accounts.
Leave 'Automatically manage signing' ticked — a free Apple ID cannot do it any other way.

An error naming HealthKit means a free Apple ID can't get that entitlement (Apple's restriction). Build without it: SKIP_HEALTHKIT=1 npm run prebuild, then reopen the workspace and set your unique Bundle Identifier again (prebuild regenerates ios/ and resets it to com.nutai.app). A paid developer account restores Health sync.

steps.title: Install Java 17
steps.body: The Android build needs a JDK 17 to 21, not only a Java runtime. Installs Temurin 17 if none.
steps.command:
rm -f ~/.nut-ai-java-home
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/bin/javac" ] && "$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | grep -Eq 'version "(1[7-9]|2[01])[."]'; then echo "$JAVA_HOME" > ~/.nut-ai-java-home; fi
[ -s ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] || find -L /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines ~/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines ~/.nut-ai-jdk -maxdepth 5 -path '*/Contents/Home/bin/java' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r j; do [ -x "${j%/java}/javac" ] && "$j" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | grep -Eq 'version "17[."]' && echo "${j%/bin/java}" > ~/.nut-ai-java-home && break; done
[ -s ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] || find -L /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines ~/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines ~/.nut-ai-jdk -maxdepth 5 -path '*/Contents/Home/bin/java' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r j; do [ -x "${j%/java}/javac" ] && "$j" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | grep -Eq 'version "(1[89]|2[01])[."]' && echo "${j%/bin/java}" > ~/.nut-ai-java-home && break; done
if [ ! -s ~/.nut-ai-java-home ]; then
  uname -m | grep -q arm64 && NUT_AI_JDK_ARCH=aarch64 NUT_AI_JDK_SHA=78b08c7f5a0598242d5719c022e19479cb4a3aa45c37c19726a757a469ed1c15 || NUT_AI_JDK_ARCH=x64 NUT_AI_JDK_SHA=868f5c672b3389fdbe48e44f94ae170f01668b1401360944fc7159d7cc9772cc
  curl -fL --retry 3 -o ~/.nut-ai-jdk.tar.gz "https://api.adoptium.net/v3/binary/version/jdk-17.0.21%2B9/mac/$NUT_AI_JDK_ARCH/jdk/hotspot/normal/eclipse"
  echo "$NUT_AI_JDK_SHA  $HOME/.nut-ai-jdk.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c - && mkdir -p ~/.nut-ai-jdk && tar -xzf ~/.nut-ai-jdk.tar.gz -C ~/.nut-ai-jdk && "$HOME/.nut-ai-jdk/jdk-17.0.21+9/Contents/Home/bin/java" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | grep -Eq 'version "17[."]' && echo "$HOME/.nut-ai-jdk/jdk-17.0.21+9/Contents/Home" > ~/.nut-ai-java-home
  rm -f ~/.nut-ai-jdk.tar.gz
fi
read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME
"$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version
[ -x "$JAVA_HOME/bin/javac" ] && "$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version 2>&1 | grep -Eq 'version "(1[7-9]|2[01])[."]' || { echo 'No JDK 17 to 21 is ready. Install the Temurin 17 JDK from adoptium.net, then run this step again.'; false; }

expect.prompt: Does the last java -version output in the terminal show a version from 17 to 21 (openjdk version "17..." to "21..."), not 1.8, 11 or 24 and newer?

hints: winget missing? Install the Temurin 17 JDK (not the JRE) from adoptium.net, then run this step again.
Other Java versions can stay installed: the build uses only the Java this step picks.

steps.title: Turn on USB debugging
steps.body: Settings → About phone → tap Build number 7×. Then Developer options → USB debugging.
steps.verifierLabel: Developer options shows USB debugging on

steps.title: Plug in your phone
steps.body: Tap Allow on the phone. If nothing appears, try another cable — that is the usual cause.
steps.verifierLabel: adb devices lists your phone

steps.title: Generate the Android project
steps.command: npx.cmd expo prebuild --platform android
steps.verifierLabel: An android folder appears inside apps/mobile

steps.title: Download the Android build tools
steps.body: The first run downloads Gradle and the Android NDK. Later runs take about a minute.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the C++ code, part 1 of 3
steps.body: Compiles C++ code for your phone's processor only. Keep the phone plugged in until the end.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the C++ code, part 2 of 3
steps.body: Compiles the C++ code of the animation libraries.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the C++ code, part 3 of 3
steps.body: Compiles the app's own C++ code. This is the longest build step.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the Kotlin and Java code
steps.body: Compiles the libraries' Kotlin and Java code.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Check and convert the libraries
steps.body: Checks the libraries for release errors and converts them to Android code.
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build and install
steps.body: Builds the app, installs it on your phone and opens it.
steps.verifierLabel: The build ends with an install onto your phone

steps.title: Open Nut AI on your phone
steps.body: Scans run on publik API; link the phone when asked. Your own AI key also works (Profile).
steps.verifierLabel: Nut AI opens on your phone

unsupported.headline: A Windows PC cannot build an iPhone app
unsupported.reason: Apple only allows iPhone apps to be built and signed on macOS using Xcode, which Apple does not release for Windows. This is Apple's restriction, not a missing feature in Nut AI or Iris — no setup, emulator, or virtual machine makes it work reliably.
alternatives: Borrow a Mac for about thirty minutes — the signature it installs lasts 7 days and can be renewed on any Mac.
Use an Android phone instead, which builds fine from Windows.
